minutes.headline: Commission agreed to press the Town Manager on stalled Ritter and Town Hall work and approved streamlined design guidelines.
minutes.summary: The commission voted to adopt the simplified design guidelines after a public hearing, including a new preliminary determination of applicability form. Members discussed the lack of progress on the Ritter Memorial Building and Town Hall projects and agreed the chair will draft a note to the Town Manager's office. They also debated expanding the district or merging with the Historical Commission, and agreed to consult Town Counsel again.

votes.motion: Approve the meeting minutes as amended (call for ayes; minutes declared approved pending changes)
Approve the amendments to the design guidelines (roll call: Richard aye, Nathan aye, chair aye)

budget_items.what_was_said: The single bid received was excessively high and no rebid has happened; phasing the work was discussed but not acted on.
The chair feared an updated estimate would show insufficient funds, possibly delaying any bid until after a special town meeting.
A member suggested the project might be eligible for historic rehabilitation grant funding.
Members noted labour and material inflation driven by infrastructure funding, so waiting raises cost.
Town Counsel said giving state-derived money to homeowners would need a special appropriation and a town meeting vote.
The consultant's proposed development plan is state-funded with a deadline in mid to late June.
A member found a federal historic credit and some state credits and will keep researching.

decisions.decision: The chair will draft a note on Ritter Memorial/Town Hall progress to the facilities manager, copying the Town Manager, after circulating it to members.
Revised design guidelines are effective as of this date; the chair will ask the webmaster to post them with the two forms as standalone attachments and explore making the PDF form fillable.
Members agreed to talk to Town Counsel (Adam Costa) about expanding the district, merging with the Historical Commission, and a road map of priorities.
Chair to finish property owner notification and brochure and present at the June meeting.
Next meeting set for the 13th of June at 7:30.

what_happened.line: The commission voted 3-0 to adopt the amended design guidelines after a public hearing, effective that date.
Members agreed the chair will draft a note on the stalled Ritter Memorial and Town Hall projects to the facilities manager, copying the Town Manager.
The single Town Hall renovation bid was described as excessively high, with no rebid and phasing discussed but not acted on.
Members agreed to consult Town Counsel again on expanding the district, merging with the Historical Commission, and a priorities road map.
Town Counsel's view, as relayed, was that passing state-derived money to homeowners would need a special appropriation and a town meeting vote.

why_it_matters: The Ritter Memorial Building and Town Hall work are town-owned buildings, and the minutes describe cost rising with delay, so a later bid or a special town meeting article could ask residents for more money.
Owners of buildings in the district work under the revised guidelines and the new preliminary determination form, and any plan to help homeowners with money would need a town meeting vote.
